envelope.description: Stamp the range base at approval, gated on the artifact's workflow, as a declared full sha

body.title: Stamp the range base at approval, gated on the artifact's workflow, as a declared full sha
body.summary: Write meta.rangeBase (HEAD at approval time) at the single approval site. s1 established three constraints the LLD could not: approveArtifactByJsonPath (gates.ts:499) is GENERIC across every artifact kind, so the stamp MUST be gated on meta.workflow rather than written unconditionally onto DEF/HLD/AMD/BUILD records; it is SYNCHRONOUS, so an await-based read cannot go there; and the base must be a FULL sha, since an abbreviation in a persisted range base can collide as history grows and a base that silently resolves to the wrong commit is the exact class of defect this ISSUE exists to remove. CRITIQUE APPLIED — the MECHANISM is now named rather than left to the build: run `git rev-parse HEAD` WITHOUT `--short` through the directory's existing synchronous execFileSync idiom (migrate-docs-tree.ts:317, tracker/github.ts:17) inside gates.ts. Do NOT call revParse (helpers.ts:40), which hard-codes `--short` and would silently persist an abbreviation that satisfies the letter of the stamp while defeating it; and do NOT widen revParse, whose eleven-plus git-builtin call sites all want the short form. The field must also be DECLARED, not merely written: gates.ts:504-512 parses meta through a narrow inline literal type, and under strict mode with exactOptionalPropertyTypes an undeclared field is at best unchecked and invisible to every downstream reader. Inert until t6 reads it.
acceptanceChecks: meta.rangeBase is DECLARED on the artifact-meta type gates.ts parses, as an optional `string | undefined` matching the repo's exactOptionalPropertyTypes convention, and that declaration is the single source every reader uses — no inline cast at the read site

Approving a PLAN stamps meta.rangeBase alongside meta.approvedAt, and the stamped value MATCHES /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ — the length assertion is the only thing that mechanically distinguishes a full sha from revParse's abbreviated form
The stamp is produced by `git rev-parse HEAD` with no `--short`, via the synchronous execFileSync idiom already used in src/workflow/; revParse is NOT called and NOT modified
Approving a DEF, HLD, AMD or BUILD record stamps NO rangeBase — asserted per kind, because the stamp site is generic and an ungated stamp would pollute every artifact
A standalone-Small LLD IS stamped, being the only upstream that route has
An unreadable HEAD (non-git directory, or git unavailable) leaves rangeBase ABSENT and still completes the approval — never throws, never writes an empty string

The field survives a write-read-write round trip through approveArtifactByJsonPath; the spread at :537 preserves unknown keys, but the function also deliberately DELETES two keys immediately after, so this is pinned rather than assumed
meta.approvedAt, the rejection-clearing behaviour at gates.ts:539-540, and the review gate that precedes it are all undisturbed

tests.name: approving a PLAN in a real repo stamps meta.rangeBase alongside meta.approvedAt and the value MATCHES /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ — a full sha, not revParse's abbreviation
the generic stamp site is GATED: approving a DEF, HLD, AMD and BUILD record each stamps NO rangeBase — one assertion per kind
a standalone-Small LLD IS stamped, being the only upstream the no-plan route has
an unreadable HEAD leaves rangeBase ABSENT and still completes the approval — never throws, never writes an empty string
meta.rangeBase survives a write-read-write round trip through approveArtifactByJsonPath, and the two deliberate key deletions do not take it with them
meta.approvedAt, rejection-clearing and the preceding review gate are undisturbed by the stamp
